abstract: The lecture describes the brainstem: its three parts (midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata), their embryological origin, their external landmarks and their connections with the cerebellum, and where each cranial nerve from III to XII emerges. It also covers the internal organisation (tracts, reticular formation and fourth ventricle), the blood supply from the basilar artery, and the alternating syndrome used to locate a brainstem lesion.

concepts.name: Brainstem
concepts.definition: The stalk connecting the cerebrum to the spinal cord and cerebellum, made of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata. It lies in the posterior cranial fossa on the clivus and runs vital functions such as breathing, heart rate, blood pressure and consciousness.

evidence.quote: The brainstem is the stalk connecting the cerebrum to the spinal cord
It is composed of 3 sections in descending order: the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata

concepts.name: Midbrain
concepts.definition: The smallest part of the brainstem, about 2 cm long, passing through the tentorial opening. It has two parts: the tectum behind the cerebral aqueduct and the paired cerebral peduncles.

evidence.quote: The smallest part, about 2 cm, passing through the tentorial opening
The midbrain is the smallest of the three regions of the brainstem

concepts.name: Pons
concepts.definition: The largest part of the brainstem. Its ventral bulge, about 2.5 cm, is made by transverse pontocerebellar fibres, and the basilar groove on it holds the basilar artery.

evidence.quote: Its ventral bulge, about 2.5 cm, is made by transverse pontocerebellar fibres
Pons: largest; basilar artery in the basilar groove

concepts.name: Medulla oblongata
concepts.definition: The lowest part of the brainstem, bearing the pyramids and olives on its ventral surface and containing the respiratory and cardiovascular centres.

evidence.quote: Medulla: pyramids (corticospinal), olives (inferior olivary nucleus)
the respiratory and cardiovascular centres are in the medulla

concepts.name: Mesencephalon
concepts.definition: The third embryonic brain vesicle, which forms the midbrain.

evidence.quote: Midbrain | Mesencephalon (third vesicle)
the mesencephalon (third vesicle)

concepts.name: Metencephalon
concepts.definition: The fourth embryonic brain vesicle, which forms the pons together with the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Pons | Metencephalon (fourth vesicle)
The largest part, from the metencephalon with the cerebellum

concepts.name: Myelencephalon
concepts.definition: The fifth embryonic brain vesicle, which forms the medulla oblongata.

evidence.quote: Medulla oblongata | Myelencephalon (fifth vesicle)
the myelencephalon (fifth vesicle)

concepts.name: Cerebellar peduncle
concepts.definition: One of three paired bundles connecting the brainstem to the cerebellum behind it: superior to the midbrain, middle to the pons and inferior to the medulla.

evidence.quote: Cerebellar peduncles: superior to midbrain, middle to pons, inferior to medulla
Each part of brainstem is connected to cerebellum by cerebellar peduncles

concepts.name: Superior cerebellar peduncle
concepts.definition: The cerebellar peduncle that connects the midbrain with the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Superior peduncle connects midbrain with cerebellum

concepts.name: Middle cerebellar peduncle
concepts.definition: The cerebellar peduncle that connects the pons with the cerebellum; the largest of the three.

evidence.quote: Middle peduncle connects pons with cerebellum
middle → pons (largest)

concepts.name: Inferior cerebellar peduncle
concepts.definition: The cerebellar peduncle that connects the medulla oblongata with the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Inferior peduncle connects medulla oblongata with cerebellum

concepts.name: Tectum
concepts.definition: The part of the midbrain behind the cerebral aqueduct, carrying two superior and two inferior colliculi below the pineal gland.

evidence.quote: Tectum, behind the cerebral aqueduct: two superior and two inferior colliculi below the pineal gland
Tectum: located posterior to the cerebral aqueduct

concepts.name: Superior colliculus
concepts.definition: One of the upper pair of rounded prominences of the tectum, linked to the retina by the superior brachium (vision).

evidence.quote: The superior brachium links the superior colliculus with the retina (vision)
there are two superior and two inferior colliculi

concepts.name: Inferior colliculus
concepts.definition: One of the lower pair of rounded prominences of the tectum; its fibres run with the lateral lemniscus in the inferior brachium to the medial geniculate body (hearing).

evidence.quote: the inferior brachium carries lateral lemniscus and inferior colliculus fibres to the medial geniculate body (hearing)

concepts.name: Superior brachium
concepts.definition: The pathway extending laterally from the superior colliculus that links it with the retina of the eye (vision).

evidence.quote: Superior quadrigeminal brachium forms a pathway between the superior colliculus and the retina of the eye

concepts.name: Cerebral peduncle
concepts.definition: One of the paired anterolateral parts of the midbrain, running from the cerebral hemispheres to the pons and separated from its fellow by the interpeduncular fossa. The oculomotor nerve exits between the two.

evidence.quote: Cerebral peduncles, paired and anterolateral, separated by the interpeduncular fossa
The paired cerebral peduncles extend from the cerebral hemispheres to converge as they meet the pons

concepts.name: Interpeduncular fossa
concepts.definition: The midline depression that separates the two cerebral peduncles anteriorly.

evidence.quote: They are separated anteriorly in the midline by the interpeduncular fossa

concepts.name: Tentorial opening
concepts.definition: The opening in the tentorium cerebelli through which the midbrain passes.

evidence.quote: It travels through the opening in the tentorium cerebelli

concepts.name: Cerebral aqueduct
concepts.definition: The ependymal cavity that runs through the midbrain, in front of the tectum.

evidence.quote: Aqueduct runs through the midbrain
the aqueduct passes through the midbrain

concepts.name: Fourth ventricle
concepts.definition: The ependymal cavity behind the pons and medulla. Its roof is the superior and inferior medullary vela, its floor the rhomboid fossa, and CSF leaves it by the median foramen of Magendie and the two lateral foramina of Luschka.

evidence.quote: Roof: the superior and inferior medullary vela. Floor: the rhomboid fossa
The floor, located ventrally, is formed by the rhomboid fossa

concepts.name: Rhomboid fossa
concepts.definition: The diamond-shaped depression on the dorsal surface of the pons and upper half of the medulla that forms the floor of the fourth ventricle.

evidence.quote: a diamond-shaped depression on the dorsal surface of the pons and upper half of the medulla
fourth ventricle floor is the rhomboid fossa

concepts.name: Obex
concepts.definition: The most caudal tip of the fourth ventricle.

evidence.quote: The obex is the most caudal tip of the fourth ventricle
obex at its caudal tip

concepts.name: Fastigium
concepts.definition: The peak of the fourth ventricle within the cerebellum, lying under the fastigial nucleus.

evidence.quote: The peak of the fourth ventricle within the cerebellum is the fastigium

concepts.name: Foramen of Luschka
aliases: Lateral aperture of the fourth ventricle
concepts.definition: One of the two lateral apertures of the fourth ventricle through which CSF leaves; it lies at the cerebellopontine angle.

evidence.quote: CSF leaves by the median foramen of Magendie and two lateral foramina of Luschka
lateral apertures of the fourth ventricle (the foramen of Luschka)

concepts.name: Foramen of Magendie
concepts.definition: The median foramen through which CSF leaves the fourth ventricle.

evidence.quote: CSF leaves by the median foramen of Magendie and two lateral foramina of Luschka

concepts.name: Facial colliculus
concepts.definition: A bulge on the floor of the fourth ventricle formed by fibres of the facial nerve looping around the abducens nucleus.

evidence.quote: Facial colliculus: facial fibres looping around the abducens nucleus
The facial colliculus is a bulging formed by the fibres of the facial nerve looping around the abducens nucleus

concepts.name: Stria medullaris of the fourth ventricle
concepts.definition: A bundle of nerve fibres crossing the floor of the fourth ventricle transversely; it marks the posterior border between the pons and the medulla.

evidence.quote: They mark the posterior border between the pons and the medulla
the stria medullaris marking the pons-medulla border

concepts.name: Cerebellopontine angle
concepts.definition: The angle at the junction of the pons, medulla and cerebellum, where the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves emerge beside the foramen of Luschka.

evidence.quote: Cerebellopontine angle: CN VII and VIII beside the foramen of Luschka
The angle formed at the junction of the pons, medulla, and cerebellum

concepts.name: Pontomedullary junction
concepts.definition: The landmark angle between the lower border of the pons and the upper border of the medulla, where cranial nerves VI, VII and VIII emerge from medial to lateral.

evidence.quote: defined by the angle between the lower border of the pons and the superior border of the medulla
VI, VII, VIII at the pontomedullary junction (medial to lateral)

concepts.name: Basilar groove
concepts.definition: The midline groove on the ventral surface of the pons in which the basilar artery lies.

evidence.quote: The basilar groove holds the basilar artery
The basilar groove demarcates the midline of the ventral surface

concepts.name: Basilar artery
concepts.definition: The artery lying in the basilar groove of the pons; with its branches it supplies the brainstem.

evidence.quote: The brainstem receives vascular supply from the basilar artery and its branches
Supplied by the basilar artery and its branches

concepts.name: Posterior cerebral artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the basilar artery which, with its peduncular branch, helps supply the brainstem.

evidence.quote: the posterior cerebral artery and its peduncular branch

concepts.name: Superior cerebellar artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the basilar artery that helps supply the brainstem.

evidence.quote: Superior cerebellar artery

concepts.name: Pyramid of the medulla
concepts.definition: The elevation on each side of the ventral median fissure of the medulla, produced by the corticospinal tract.

evidence.quote: The pyramid on each side is made by the corticospinal tract
Produced by corticospinal tract

concepts.name: Olive
concepts.definition: The elevation lateral to the pyramid on the medulla, produced by the inferior olivary nucleus.

evidence.quote: the olive lateral to it by the inferior olivary nucleus
An elevation, lies lateral to the pyramid

concepts.name: Inferior olivary nucleus
concepts.definition: The nucleus that produces the olive of the medulla; it is important in the control of movement.

evidence.quote: Produced by inferior olivary nucleus (important in control of movement)
Olive = inferior olivary nucleus

concepts.name: Pyramidal decussation
concepts.definition: The crossing of 75 to 90 percent of the corticospinal fibres in the lower medulla, marking the lower part of the ventral median fissure.

evidence.quote: decussation of 75 to 90 percent of corticospinal fibres
75-90% decussate in the lower medulla

concepts.name: Corticospinal tract
concepts.definition: The descending motor tract that, with the corticobulbar tract, controls voluntary movement of the body and face; it forms the pyramids of the medulla.

evidence.quote: Corticospinal and corticobulbar | Descending | Voluntary movement of body and face
composed by the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts

concepts.name: Dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway
concepts.definition: An ascending conscious tract through the brainstem carrying touch, proprioception and vibration.

evidence.quote: Dorsal column-medial lemniscus | Ascending, conscious | Touch, proprioception, vibration

concepts.name: Anterolateral system
concepts.definition: An ascending conscious tract through the brainstem carrying crude touch, pain and temperature.

evidence.quote: Anterolateral (spinothalamic) | Ascending, conscious | Crude touch, pain, temperature

concepts.name: Spinocerebellar tract
concepts.definition: An ascending unconscious tract carrying proprioception to the cerebellum.

evidence.quote: Spinocerebellar | Ascending, unconscious | Proprioception to the cerebellum

concepts.name: Reticular formation
concepts.definition: A network of neuronal cell bodies and small axon bundles without distinct boundaries, spread from the spinal cord through the brainstem to the hypothalamus and thalamus. It integrates arousal, consciousness, sleep-wake cycles, motor coordination, cardiovascular and respiratory control and pain modulation.

evidence.quote: It integrates vital functions: arousal, consciousness, sleep-wake cycles
It does not have any distinct cytoarchitectural boundaries and is dispersed throughout the brainstem

concepts.name: Respiratory and cardiovascular centres
concepts.definition: The vital centres controlling breathing and circulation, located in the medulla oblongata.

evidence.quote: the respiratory and cardiovascular centres are in the medulla
cardiovascular and respiratory centres (medulla)

concepts.name: Oculomotor nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve III, which leaves the midbrain between the two cerebral peduncles.

evidence.quote: The oculomotor nerve (CN III) is seen exiting from between the peduncles
III between the cerebral peduncles

concepts.name: Trochlear nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve IV, the only cranial nerve that emerges from the dorsal surface of the brainstem, below the inferior colliculi of the midbrain.

evidence.quote: CN IV is the only nerve emerging dorsally
which emerges from the dorsal surface of the midbrain

concepts.name: Trigeminal nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve V, which emerges from the lateral aspect of the mid-pons.

evidence.quote: CN V, trigeminal | Lateral mid-pons
trigeminal originates from the lateral aspect of mid pons

concepts.name: Abducens nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve VI, which emerges at the pontomedullary junction close to the midline.

evidence.quote: CN VI, abducens | Pontomedullary junction, near the midline
abducens originates from the pontomedullary junction, close to the midline

concepts.name: Facial nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve VII, which emerges at the cerebellopontine angle; its fibres loop around the abducens nucleus to form the facial colliculus.

evidence.quote: CN VII, facial | Cerebellopontine angle
facial originates from the cerebellopontine angle

concepts.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve VIII, which emerges lateral to the facial nerve at the cerebellopontine angle.

evidence.quote: CN VIII, vestibulocochlear | Lateral to CN VII
vestibulocochlear originates laterally to the facial nerve

concepts.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve IX, a mixed nerve that emerges from the medulla behind the olive.

evidence.quote: CN IX, X, XI behind the olive
Lateral, behind the olive | IX, X and XI, the mixed nerves

concepts.name: Vagus nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve X, a mixed nerve that emerges from the medulla behind the olive.

evidence.quote: CN IX, X, XI behind the olive
Lateral, behind the olive | IX, X and XI, the mixed nerves

concepts.name: Accessory nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve XI, which emerges from the medulla behind the olive with nerves IX and X.

evidence.quote: CN IX, X, XI behind the olive
cranial part of accessory(11th)

concepts.name: Hypoglossal nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve XII, which emerges from the medulla in the sulcus between the pyramid and the olive.

evidence.quote: CN XII between pyramid and olive
from sulcus between pyramid & olive

concepts.name: Optic nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve II, one of the two cranial nerves that do not arise from the brainstem.

evidence.quote: with the exception of two: the optic nerve and the olfactory nerve
not CN I or II

concepts.name: Olfactory nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve I, one of the two cranial nerves that do not arise from the brainstem.

evidence.quote: with the exception of two: the optic nerve and the olfactory nerve
not CN I or II

concepts.name: Posterior cranial fossa
concepts.definition: The cranial fossa in which the brainstem lies, on the clivus and under the tentorium cerebelli.

evidence.quote: It lies in the posterior cranial fossa, on the clivus, under the tentorium cerebelli

concepts.name: Transverse fissure of Bichat
concepts.definition: The fissure that marks the upper limit of the brainstem, between it and the diencephalon.

evidence.quote: Above, the diencephalon by the transverse fissure of Bichat
Above: diencephalon by transverse fissure of BICHAT

concepts.name: Alternating syndrome
concepts.definition: A cranial nerve palsy on the side of the lesion together with a hemiplegia on the opposite side. The cranial nerve involved locates the lesion to a level of the brainstem.

evidence.quote: Alternating syndrome: ipsilateral cranial nerve palsy plus contralateral hemiplegia
A peripheral cranial nerve lesion on one side with a hemiplegia on the other locates the lesion to a level in the brainstem

concepts.name: Acoustic neuroma
concepts.definition: A tumour at the cerebellopontine angle that gives unilateral deafness and tinnitus, then facial and trigeminal signs.

evidence.quote: an acoustic neuroma gives unilateral deafness, tinnitus, then facial and trigeminal signs

conflicts.issue: A slide says the trochlear nerve's muscle 'ensures upward gaze'. Standard teaching is that the superior oblique depresses and intorts the eye (downward gaze, especially in adduction).

evidence.quote: innervates the major oblique muscle of the eye: ensures upward gaze

conflicts.issue: A slide places the cephalic flexure between brainstem and spinal cord and lists the mesencephalic flexure separately. In standard embryology the cephalic flexure is the mesencephalic flexure, at the midbrain; the bend between brainstem and spinal cord is the cervical flexure.

evidence.quote: the cephalic flexure: brainstem and spinal cord

conflicts.issue: A slide says the brainstem lies in the 'posterior cerebral fossa'; the summary and the questions say posterior cranial fossa.

evidence.quote: It is located at the posterior cerebral fossa
It lies in the posterior cranial fossa

notes: The relation vocabulary has no type for 'nerve emerges from/at' or 'connects X with Y'; these are the core of this lecture and were recorded as related-to with the fact in the statement.
Slides 15 and 17 are headed 'THE MIDBRAIN' but describe the posterior pons and the medulla; treated as heading errors.

'Bulbopontine groove' is given as another name for the pontomedullary junction because the nerve table and the high-yield note describe the same emergence site under the two names; the packet never equates them outright.
